title: Raşa's logarithmic-convexity conjecture for squared Baskakov functions
statement:
For $n
in\mathbb{N}$, $c>0$, and

$$
\psi_{n,c}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left(p_{n,k}^{[c]}(x)\right)^2,
$$

where

$$
p_{n,k}^{[c]}(x)=\binom{-n/c}{k}\left(-cx\right)^k\left(1+cx\right)^{-n/c-k},\qquad x\geq 0,
$$

**Raşa's conjecture.** The function $\psi_{n,c}$ is logarithmically convex. The paper proves complete monotonicity of $\psi_{n,c}$, which implies logarithmic convexity; thus this conjecture is resolved.
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1402.6539](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6539).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.7945

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
source_name: Ulrich Abel, Wolfgang Gawronski and Thorsten Neuschel, “Complete Monotonicity and Zeros of Sums of Squared Baskakov Functions”, arXiv:1411.7945 (2014).
